samples.summary: No test renders a component that publishes a durability lapse — the 'lapse reaching the chip' suite hand-builds the scopes it claims to be wiring coverage for
samples.evidence: `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx` (~line 786) opens a block whose docblock says the earlier `tooltipFor` cases "pass whether or not `useDurabilityLapse()` ever answers anything — and it did not: `CollabDocumentProvider` mounted its own scope *inside* `DurableYorkieProvider`'s ... These drive the wiring instead of the function." But `strandedUnderScopes()` (line ~805) renders two literal `<DurabilityLapseScope>` elements around a bare `<SyncStatusChip />`. It never mounts `CollabDocumentProvider` or `DurableYorkieProvider`, so it only exercises `DurabilityLapseScope`'s inherit-when-undefined semantics. Moving the scope in collab-document-provider.tsx back inside `inner` (line 301) — the exact regression named — fails no test: `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` and `collab-document-provider-identity.test.tsx` never call `useDurabilityLapse`, and `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx`'s only probe is `useDocumentDurability()`. Consequently the call-site lapse ternary (collab-document-provider.tsx:291–299, mapping unsupported / not-permitted / not-enabled / another-tab) is also entirely unasserted, including the `not-permitted` value the chip relies on at sync-status-chip.tsx:98 to suppress the offer on a share link — that suppression is tested only with a manually supplied lapse.
searchedFor: grep "'not-permitted'|'another-tab'|'not-enabled'|'unsupported'" across packages/frontend (only chip test, tooltip, context, and the two providers match)

samples.summary: The quota → `out-of-space` lapse classification is never exercised; `onWriteFailure` is only ever driven with a plain Error
samples.evidence: `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` calls `captured[0].onWriteFailure?.(new Error('refused'))` at lines 183 and 237 and asserts only that the Probe flips to 'not-durable'. Nothing ever passes a `new DOMException('quota','QuotaExceededError')`, so the `setOutOfSpace(true)` branch (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:164–169) and the `outOfSpace ? 'out-of-space'` arm of the lapse ternary (line 219) are dead to the suite. The chip test asserts the `out-of-space` sentence only by handing `tooltipFor`/a manual scope the string. The design requires the tooltip to name which case applies; a broken classification would silently degrade the one actionable message ('out of local storage space') to the generic 'could not be written to' with every test green.

samples.summary: The `saved-locally` toast's `warned.current` latch and its retraction/confirmation on recovery are untested
samples.evidence: The new `savedLocally` arm sets `warned.current = true` (sync-status-chip.tsx:181) specifically so "the recovery arm below retracts this one too and confirms once the work actually reaches the server". The durable suite in `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx` ('says where the work went instead of saying nothing') only asserts `toast.info` fired; no case drives saved-locally → saved and asserts `toast.dismiss(TOAST_ID)` plus the 'Saved' confirmation, though the equivalent transition is covered for the `stranded` path. Impact is contained (the info toast has a finite duration), but the latch could stop working undetected.
searchedFor: grep 'dismiss' and 'RECOVERY_TOAST_ID' in the chip test

samples.summary: The `restoreAppendedChanges` throw fallback in `rehydrateArchive` — rebuilding from the snapshot alone — has no test
samples.evidence: `offline-copy.ts` wraps the replay in a try/catch that, on failure, rebuilds a *fresh* `Document.fromBytes` and returns `{complete: false, replayed: 0}` (comment: "a half-applied root is the one thing worse than a stale one"). `offline-copy.test.ts` covers a gap in the log, a JSON-undecodable entry, a missing head and a whole log — all of which truncate *before* `restoreAppendedChanges` is called — but nothing makes the replay itself throw. If that fallback regressed, a partially-bad archive would throw out of recovery instead of returning the snapshot, and `offline-runtime` would report 'Could not recover those changes' for work it could still have handed back.
searchedFor: read the 'a log that is not whole' describe block in offline-copy.test.ts

samples.summary: `snapshotWatermark`'s undefined fallback (doc missing `getPendingChangesAfter`/`getCheckpoint`) and the resulting neighbour-only contiguity path are untested
samples.evidence: `snapshotWatermark` returns `undefined` for a document that cannot answer, and `rehydrateArchive` then falls back to neighbour-only contiguity (`expected` starts undefined). Every case in `offline-copy.test.ts` builds a real `Document` from `@yorkie-js/sdk`, so `watermark` is always a number — the weaker fallback branch, which is precisely the one that would report a head-missing log as `complete`, never runs. The 'refuses a log whose head is missing' case pins the watermark path only.

samples.summary: `belongsToAnotherUser` — the cross-account guard on orphan-snapshot collection — is never exercised
samples.evidence: `orphanSnapshotKeys()` filters out keys whose `wb:{secret}:{userId}:` segment names another account. `wafflebase-doc-store-atomicity.test.ts`'s 'an entry that predates the header rule' seeds the key `"doc-a"`, which matches the regex not at all, so the guard is inert in the only test that reaches this code. No test seeds an orphan under `pk/wb:secret:user-2:sheet-x/sheet-x` and asserts this user's sweep leaves it alone (nor that it does collect its own). A regex regression would either silently delete another account's snapshot or leave the leak the branch exists to bound.

samples.summary: The route-param assertion was weakened from every-URL to some-URL, so a call that drops its id entirely now passes on a companion request
samples.evidence: The loop previously asserted `expect(pathname).toContain(encodeURIComponent(TRAVERSAL))` for every request a call emitted; it is now `paths.some(...)`. The traversal check survives per-URL, so raw-id smuggling is still caught — but the positive half no longer pins that the *named* route carried the id. `removeMember` and `deleteWorkspace` now each fire a companion `fetchWorkspace`/`fetchDocuments` that carries the encoded id, so if `removeMember`'s own DELETE stopped including the member id (or hit the wrong path), this case would still be green. Narrowing to the request actually under test (e.g. filter by method, or assert the encoded id appears in the non-companion path) would keep the old strength.

samples.summary: 'keeps a connector attached to a group member' asserts the endpoint equals its own input id
samples.evidence: `mapDescendants` maps `child-1 → child-1`, so `expect(connector.start.elementId).toBe('child-1')` re-asserts the input and would hold for any implementation that simply left the endpoint alone. The load-bearing assertion is `expect(result.droppedConnectors).toBe(0)` on the line above (without `mapDescendants` the connector is dropped and `calls[2]` would not exist), so the case is not vacuous overall — but the id assertion adds nothing, and recursion deeper than one level (`mapDescendants` calls itself) is untested.

samples.summary: The control case renders the mocked `CollabDocumentProvider`, not the real one
samples.evidence: The suite mocks `@/components/collab-document-provider` wholesale (line ~24), so `render(<CollabDocumentProvider docKey="sheet-7" />)` in 'is the route saying so, not the default' renders the probe stub and asserts the *context default* is `true`. That is a legitimate control for the probe, but the test name reads as though it validates the real provider; it cannot fail if `CollabDocumentProvider` itself stops permitting durability.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The lapse context has exactly two publishers (collab-document-provider.tsx:350 and durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:238) and one real consumer (SyncStatusChip via useDurabilityLapse). The only test touching the context, sync-status-chip.test.tsx:782-859, hand-builds two literal <DurabilityLapseScope> elements around a bare <SyncStatusChip /> (strandedUnderScopes, :797-821) despite a docblock claiming it "drives the wiring" — it never mounts CollabDocumentProvider or DurableYorkieProvider, so it tests only the scope's inherit/override semantics. The tests that do mount the real provider (collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:146-152 renders only a bare child; collab-document-provider.test.tsx:21-23 explicitly defers nesting elsewhere; durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx has no lapse probe, its "unsupported" hits at :258/:263 are a fake-doc param) never observe a lapse, and shared-document-durability.test.tsx:24-31 mocks CollabDocumentProvider away entirely. SyncStatusChip is rendered in only four test files, none under those providers, and the tooltip phrases appear in no other test. So the call-site ternary at collab-document-provider.tsx:291-299 — including the 'not-permitted' value the chip uses at sync-status-chip.tsx:98 to suppress the offline offer on a share link — and the scope's placement outside `inner` are entirely unasserted. That is a missing test over new, user-visible behavior: major under the test-adequacy rubric.

searchedFor: read durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx fakeDoc() and the mockDoc lifecycle
finding.summary: No test drives DurableLossWatch's throw-guards, though an unguarded throw there unmounts every collaborative editor
finding.evidence:
`DurableLossWatch` is rendered unconditionally by `CollabDocumentProvider` for every collaborative document (collab-document-provider.tsx:308). It carries three defences added by this diff: the doc-like-stub guard (`typeof doc.subscribe !== 'function' || typeof doc.getKey !== 'function'`, line 258), the `watch()` try/catch around each `doc.subscribe(...)` — justified in the comment at lines 260-267 with "`subscribe` does not merely ignore an event name it does not know — it *throws* ... A throw out of a passive effect propagates through render and takes the whole editor subtree with it" — and the try/catch around each `unsubscribe()` in the cleanup (lines 300-310).

Nothing exercises any of them. In `packages/frontend/src/components/__tests__/collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` the mocked `doc.subscribe` (lines 55-65) always records and returns a function; it never throws for an unknown event name, and the mocked `doc` always has both `subscribe` and `getKey`. In `packages/frontend/src/components/durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` `fakeDoc()` (lines ~/`subscribe: (type, cb) => {...}`) likewise never throws, and `mockDoc` is only ever `undefined` or a full fake — which exercises the `!doc` early return but not the stub guard. I grepped `packages/frontend` for tests that make `subscribe` throw (`Unsupported event type`, `subscribe.*throw`, `mockImplementation(() => { throw`) and found none touching this component.

So removing or inverting any of these three guards leaves the whole suite green, while on a pinned `@yorkie-js/react` that does not know `local-changes-dropped`/`persist-disabled` the result is a blank editor rather than a chip that merely loses its certainty — exactly the outcome the comment says the guard exists to prevent.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test drives DurableLossWatch's three throw-guards. durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx has a dedicated describe block (lines 256-346) that does exactly that. A `refusingDoc(...unsupported)` helper (258-269) throws `Unsupported event type: ${type}` from `subscribe`, mimicking the SDK. Tests then cover: loss-event refusal latching `expectLoss('sheet-7')` and lowering durability (271-283); persist-disabled refusal lowering durability with `expectedLosses` empty (285-295); both refused without throwing (297-304); the doc-like-stub guard via `mockDoc = { getKey: () => 'sheet-7' }` asserting no throw and durability retained (306-313), which would fail if the `typeof doc.subscribe !== 'function'` guard at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:276 were removed; and a throwing `unsubscribe` with `expect(() => view.unmount()).not.toThrow()` (315-329), covering the cleanup try/catch at lines 350-360. The reviewer's assertions that `fakeDoc()` never throws and `mockDoc` is only undefined-or-full-fake are both contradicted by this block, and their `Unsupported event type` grep would have hit line 264.

mergedFrom.summary: The cleanup-side try/catch (an `unsubscribe` that throws during teardown) is untested

finding.summary: The new `watch()` try/catch around `doc.subscribe` — the entire point of this delta's provider change — has no test where `subscribe` throws
finding.evidence: The delta wraps both subscriptions because `subscribe` throws `YorkieError(ErrInvalidArgument, 'Unsupported event type')` on SDK versions that don't know these events, and a throw out of the effect would take down the editor subtree. Both suites that exercise `DurableLossWatch` use fake docs whose `subscribe` accepts any event name and never throws: `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx:74-81` (`subscribe: (type, cb) => { handlers.set(...); return () => ... }`) and `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:55-65`. So the guarded path is never executed — deleting the try/catch (or catching the wrong thing) leaves every test green while the real failure it exists for (the whole collaborative document unmounting on an older SDK) ships undetected. There is also no test that when the first subscription throws the second is still attempted, and that the already-registered unsubscribers are still collected/cleaned up.

verdict.reason: The claim that no test exercises the watch() try/catch with a throwing subscribe is false. durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx defines refusingDoc() (lines 258-269) whose subscribe throws `Unsupported event type: ${type}` — the exact SDK failure the guard exists for — and a full describe block drives it: loss event refused asserts both lowered durability and the expectLoss latch (271-283); persist-disabled refused asserts lowered durability with empty expectedLosses, which also demonstrates execution continued past the first subscription into the second watch() (285-295); both refused asserts render does not throw (297-304); a doc-stub with no subscribe (306-313); and an unsubscribe that throws during teardown asserting unmount does not throw, covering the collected-unsubscriber cleanup (315-329). Assertions are non-vacuous: they observe durable/not-durable via useDocumentDurability and the recorded expectLoss keys through the real DurableLossWatch effect. The suite is executed — vite.config.ts:459-464 includes src/**/*.test.tsx. The reviewer's cited grep for 'throw|Unsupported' in this very file is contradicted by line 264.

finding.summary: `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` changed from swallow-and-return-0 to propagating the failure, and no unit test pins the new contract
finding.evidence: The delta removes the `catch { console.warn(...); return 0; }` from `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` so the caller's recovery gate can distinguish 'reconciled' from 'failed'. `packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-erase.test.ts` (the `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` describe block, lines ~460-551) has no case where `storedDocumentIds`/`purgeDocument` fails; every assertion is on a resolved count. Nothing fails if someone restores the swallow — and if it is restored, the runtime gate opens on a reconcile that never happened, which is exactly the harm (offering an archive from a workspace the user was removed from) the change exists to prevent. The runtime-level test 'offers nothing back when the purge itself failed' mocks `@/lib/offline-erase` wholesale (offline-runtime.test.tsx:20-28), so it cannot cover the real function. Also untested: that `store.close()` in the `finally` still runs on the throwing path.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no unit test pins the new throwing contract of `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments`. Two such tests exist, in a describe block named "access somebody else ended" (offline-erase.test.ts:457) rather than after the function name, which is why the reviewer's greps missed them. offline-erase.test.ts:506-531 ("throws when it could not enumerate what is stored") spies WafflebaseDocStore.prototype.storedDocumentIds to reject and asserts `await expect(purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments(["kept"])).rejects.toThrow(failed)` (line 521), plus that the seeded content is still on disk (528-530). offline-erase.test.ts:533-555 ("throws when a delete fails part way through") does the same for purgeDocument, asserting rejects.toThrow at line 547 and surviving content at 552-554. The comments at 506-511 and 533-537 explicitly name the recovery gate as the reason. These are not over-mocked: the real function is imported (line 10) and exercised against the real WafflebaseDocStore over fake-indexeddb (lines 1-3, 462/512/538), with only the single failing store method stubbed and restored. Restoring the swallow-and-return-0 would fail both assertions. The residual sub-claim that `store.close()` in the finally is not separately asserted on the throwing path is a contained internal-resource detail, not blocking under the test-adequacy rubric, and does not support the finding's headline claim.
